source.text: Let M be a compact smooth manifold of dimension n, and let E be a smooth finite-rank vector bundle over M with a fiber metric. If s is real, 1<p<infinity, and sp>n, then W^(s,p)(M,E) embeds continuously into L-infinity(M,E), and every section in that Sobolev space has a continuous representative.
qualifications: C0 component only; not a quotation of a full Cm embedding theorem.
For tensor sections use their smooth finite-rank tensor bundle; p=2 and sufficiently high integer s are specializations.
Historical tensorPouSobolevHilbert graph-norm correspondence not certified.

source.text: Let X be a Banach space and let f belong to L1(0,T;X). The function f has an integrable weak derivative g if and only if there is a constant c0 such that f(t)=c0+integral_0^t g(s) ds for almost every t. In this case the strong derivative exists almost everywhere and agrees with g.
qualifications: The derivative g is the actual weak derivative of f, not an arbitrary unrelated function.
The source asserts almost-everywhere differentiability; no everywhere-at-zero upgrade is attributed to the source.
Continuous weak derivative yields pointwise differentiability by the fundamental theorem, but that corollary is not represented as an original quotation.
source.selected_target_scope: Only the forward implication: an integrable weak derivative g of f agrees with the strong derivative almost everywhere. The full if-and-only-if is source context, not the selected task.

source.author: Jérémie Joudioux
source.locator: Appendix A, pp.20–21, Theorem A.1; m=1 and j=0
source.text: Let X and Y be Hilbert spaces, with X continuously and densely embedded in Y. For a finite interval [a,b], if u belongs to L2([a,b];X) and its distributional time derivative belongs to L2([a,b];Y), then u has a bounded continuous representative taking values in the interpolation space [X,Y]_(1/2).
qualifications: Specialization of independently printed m-th derivative trace theorem to m=1,j=0.
The embedding must be dense and continuous; an arbitrary continuous linear map is insufficient.
No graph-norm formula is invented or attributed to this theorem; continuous trace-space membership is the selected target.
This research paper reproduces classical Lions–Magenes, citing LM72 Chapter1 Theorems2.3,3.1; the original 1972 book was not downloaded.

source.text: For a closed connected R-oriented n-manifold M, the map from H_n(M;R) to H_n(M,M minus {x};R) is an isomorphism for every x. A class mapping to local generators everywhere is a fundamental class. Such a class exists for a closed R-oriented manifold; conversely, existence forces compactness and an R-orientation.
